hints: Look carefully at the start and the end of each curve. At the very start enzyme meets excess substrate, and at the very end all that small excess of substrate will be used up, so what must happen to ES complex?
Remember the sequence $E + S \rightarrow ES \rightarrow E + P$. With only a small excess of substrate, ES forms almost instantly to a maximum and then must fall back to zero as substrate runs out.
walkthrough:
**Picture what is happening at time 0**

Think side by side with the molecules. You add enzyme to substrate that is in small excess. Free enzyme very quickly finds substrate and forms ES complex.

So on the time scale of the whole reaction, $[ES]$ jumps almost instantly from zero to a high maximum value.

**Picture what happens during and at the end**

As the reaction proceeds, ES is constantly broken down to release product and free enzyme:
$$E + S \rightarrow ES \rightarrow E + P$$
Because there is only a small excess of substrate, substrate soon runs out. With no $S$ left to make new ES, existing ES breaks down and $[ES]$ must fall to zero.

**Match this shape to the graphs**

We need a curve that starts high (after that instant formation), stays briefly steady, then falls smoothly to zero on the time axis. That is exactly graph D. It shows the rapid saturation followed by depletion as substrate is consumed.

options.A: Shows a slow rise to a peak then a fall that never reaches zero. This does not fit a small amount of substrate being completely used up, where [ES] must end at zero.
options.B: Shows concentration rising continuously and levelling off. That is the shape for product formation, not for ES complex which must fall when substrate runs out.
options.C: Shows a flat horizontal line. ES complex cannot stay constant forever because substrate is consumed and ES is broken down to product.
options.D: Correct. ES forms almost instantly to a maximum (shown as starting high), then declines to zero as the small excess of substrate is used up and no new ES can form. Well done for spotting this.
